## Appearance

Harcourt is a small educator who features a distinctive combination of reddish or crimson hair, a small pointed chin, and a freckled nose. Her hair is sleek, glossy, and styled in a lengthy plait. She is also notable for her large, sweet, luminous eyes and glowing, rosy cheeks.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P32](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0032), [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P33](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0033), [v1 CHAPTER XXIX. ## Personality

Ann Harcourt possesses an extremely poor temper, which she is required to learn to control. She strongly believes in the holiness of obligations that have been undertaken.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P46](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0046), [v4 CHAPTER 30 LORNA DECIDES P28](../source/v04-c30.md#nw-v04-c30-p0028)_

## History

Harcourt was born in [Harborough](../codex/places.md#harborough), [Nova Scotia](../codex/places.md#nova-scotia). By the time of Dr. and Mrs. Carrow's return from a three-month trip to [Europe](../codex/places.md#europe), she had spent fourteen years living at [Grey Shutters](../codex/places.md#grey-shutters). While at [Hollowmere](../codex/places.md#hollowmere), [Nell Harcourt](../character/nell-harcourt.md) sat on the porch with [Tabitha](../character/tabitha.md) and discussed local gossip with visiting [Winifred Tolley](../character/winifred-tolley.md), including the troubled marriage of Mrs. [Pettifer](../character/pettifer.md) Miller. She also learned from [Winifred](../character/winifred-tolley.md) and [Tabitha](../character/tabitha.md) about the chaotic household and humorous mishaps surrounding the newly arrived [Presbyterian](../codex/factions.md#presbyterian) minister, John Knox Ashdown, and his four untamed children. Later, when Miss Winifred came to complain about a scandalous letter by [Grace Ashdown](../character/grace.md) published in the local paper, Harcourt passionately defended the Ashdown family, arguing that the town should celebrate their talents and virtues, which successfully inspired Miss Winifred to change her perspective.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER V. Nell’s History P11](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0011), [v4 CHAPTER 4 THE FIRST BRIDE OF GREY SHUTTERS P16](../source/v04-c04.md#nw-v04-c04-p0016), [v5 CHAPTER I. HOME AGAIN P1](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0001), [v5 CHAPTER I. HOME AGAIN P2](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0002), [v5 CHAPTER I. HOME AGAIN P8](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0008), [v5 CHAPTER I. HOME AGAIN P12](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0012), +7 more_

## Quotes

> "I could assist you so greatly at present and save you effort in numerous manners. For that single reason, I could truly desire to have been one."
>
> — Harcourt — [v1 CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream P40](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0040)

> "If I were traveling by car, I would bring you. However, I plan to go on foot, a distance too great for legs belonging to an eight-year-old. Furthermore, Cedric will accompany me, and I suspect his presence does not bring you pleasure."
>
> — Harcourt — [v2 XXVII An Afternoon at the Stone House P4](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0004)

> "Upon seeing him on the playground, he was so soaked that I dispatched him straight home to get dressed before I could learn the reason."
>
> — Harcourt — [v2 XXVII An Afternoon at the Stone House P6](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0006)

> "Emptiness is the absolute worst thing . . . and my departure from your existence is not happening. Letters and vacations do exist, after all. My dear, you appear somewhat pale and exhausted, I fear."
>
> — Harcourt — [v2 XXVII An Afternoon at the Stone House P33](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0033)

> "Belinda, it seems to me that Miss Rosalind requires a change of scenery. Her time spent here in solitude is far too great. Is there no way we can persuade her to take a short journey?"
>
> — Harcourt — [v2 XXVII An Afternoon at the Stone House P46](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0046)

### [Miss Pembroke](../character/miss-pembroke.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/harcourt--miss-pembroke.md)

[Miss Pembroke](../character/miss-pembroke.md) is a frequent visitor and favorite companion of Harcourt at [Beechwood](../codex/places.md#beechwood). Their close connection has endured since the first volume.

### [Belinda](../character/belinda.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/belinda--harcourt.md)

[Belinda](../character/belinda.md) and Harcourt are close friends who reside in the same household. Harcourt frequently interacts with her during visits to [Echo Cottage](../codex/places.md#echo-cottage), sharing meals, picking strawberries, and assisting with wedding preparations for Miss Rosalind.

### [Cedric Stanhope](../character/cedric-stanhope.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/cedric-stanhope--harcourt.md)

Harcourt served as an instructor to [Cedric Stanhope](../character/cedric-stanhope.md), who quickly became a favorite student. Their bond developed through local walks, shared visits to [Echo Cottage](../codex/places.md#echo-cottage), and discussions regarding family and romantic developments.
